title: Harvest Labs POC - cost guardrails and benchmark scoping
summary: Discovery + POC scoping focused on unit economics: per-token estimates, batching and prefix/KV caching knobs, budget guardrails. Agreed to a 6-week pilot with staged benchmarks (synthetic perf + live workload) and a cap on spend. Redwood to deliver cost model spreadsheet and benchmark plan; Harvest to provide sample prompt set and traffic profile.
topics: workload sizing - qps, avg tokens, peak patterns
per-token cost estimates and quantization tradeoffs
benchmark plan - synthetic vs live, metrics to capture
timeline and budget guardrails for 6-week POC
security and deployment mode (hosted vs VPC/private)
questions: What latency SLOs do you need at 95th/p99?
How many concurrent users and peak QPS do we expect?
Is PII present in prompts; do you require on-prem/VPC?
What's your acceptable monthly spend cap for the pilot?
Do you have a prioritized prompt set for quality regression checks?
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time—I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Evan: Hey Evan here, Head of ML at Harvest.
[00:09] Sofia: Sofia, CTO.
[00:11] Liam: Liam, infra.
[00:12] Maya: Maya, product.
[00:14] Priya: Priya, I'm Redwood SE, I'll lead the bench design.
[00:18] Jordan: Awesome. The goal today is to scope a POC around cost/unit economics and a benchmark plan so you can sign off on a pilot with safe budget guardrails. We know you sent over the traffic profile, thanks.
[00:30] Evan: Yeah, we uploaded a csv; it's mostly conversational query-routing, average prompt + response about 650 tokens combined, s.d. is pretty high, some long sessions up to 3k tokens.
[00:41] Priya: Got it. Average 650 tokens per request is a helpful anchor. Quick question — is that including system prompts and embeddings calls?
[00:48] Evan: System + user + response combined. We also do embeddings for search but less frequently, about 15% of calls.
[00:55] Jordan: Cool. On cost modeling we'll break down per-token math: model choice, quantization, effective throughput with batching, and prefix/KV cache hit assumptions. Any hard budget caps for the pilot?
[01:07] Sofia: We want to limit spend to under $15k for the month of the pilot. Ideally prove a path to <$0.0015 per generated token in production for the common path.
[01:18] Priya: Okay, that's useful. For targets: are you prioritizing latency or cost? There's the usual tradeoff — bigger batches means lower cost per token but higher tail latency.
[01:27] Maya: Product leans latency—they want snappy UI, p95 under 250ms; but finance wants to see conservative cost estimates.
[01:36] Jordan: So p95 250ms is our SLO target. We'll aim benchmarks to show we can hit that at your expected QPS. Can you share peak QPS and concurrency?
[01:45] Evan: Peak around 40 QPS, steady state 8-12 QPS. Spiky bursts during office hours.
[01:52] Priya: Great. For the bench we'll simulate arrival patterns with a Poisson burst model to reproduce spikes. We'll run synthetic and replay-based tests. Synthetic is useful for tight control of batch sizes and quant modes. Replay tests will use your sample prompt set to validate real distributions.
[02:05] Liam: For deployment, security is important. We need VPC or on-prem for any PII. We can provide sanitized samples for benching but will want to evaluate VPC Private deployment later. SOC2 is a must.
[02:17] Jordan: We support SOC 2 and can run Dedicated or Private. For the POC, hosted with a VPC peering option could be fastest, unless you require airgapped.
[02:26] Sofia: Hosted with peering is fine for now. We will ask for the security pack.
[02:30] Jordan: Noted. Now the cost model basics: we estimate per-token delta = model base cost * token count / throughput efficiency. Example: for a 13B open model quantized to 4-bit, baseline is $X per 1M tokens on Redwood's hosted tier — but effective cost at your workload depends on batching efficiency and cache hit rate.
[02:48] Priya: I'll walk through an example. If average request is 650 tokens and throughput allows 20 tokens per ms per GPU (example numbers), effective cost per request at batch size 8 vs 1 changes by ~3x. Also prefix or KV cache hits reduce generation tokens; if you have many repeated prefixes (like system prompts), that can drop overall token generation by 10-30%.
[03:08] Evan: Our FAQ flows include repeated system prompts and similar context across users — likely we will see decent prefix reuse.
[03:15] Priya: Good, we'll model cache hit buckets: conservative 5%, expected 18%, optimistic 35%. We'll produce a table in the cost spreadsheet.
[03:23] Jordan: On quantization: moving from fp16 to 4-bit yields ~2-3x cost drop but may introduce small quality delta. We should include a quality regression plan — a small eval set and P50/P90 BLEU-ish or more likely ROUGE/semantic similarity checks.
[03:39] Maya: We have an internal human-rated baseline for 200 prompts. We'll share that as the prioritized prompt set.
[03:44] Jordan: Perfect. For benchmarks we propose these phases: 1) baseline synthetic latency & throughput across model variants and quantization levels, no caching; 2) introduce batching and measure batch latency distribution and p95/p99; 3) replay your sample prompt set with prefix cache simulator and measure real cost per token and quality; 4) a short live smoke test with a small percentage of real traffic if you want.
[04:05] Priya: Bench metrics: qps, tokens/s, GPU utilization, latency (p50/p95/p99), batch size distribution, cache hit rate, cost per 1k generated tokens, and output quality metrics. We'll export to a Google sheet and attach the raw perf traces.
[04:20] Liam: For the smoke live test, what are rollback/failsafe options? If latency spikes we need an automatic fallback to a cheaper hosted model or degrade to cached responses.
[04:29] Carlos: We can configure routing policies: fallback to a smaller model or serve cached responses. Redwood's routing supports per-route failsafe and region fallback. We'll show a canary plan.
[04:38] Sofia: Good. On instrumentation, we want token-level cost visibility per request. Do you expose that in console?
[04:44] Jordan: Yes—cost per token, per-route cost, and token breakdown is available. We'll show sample screenshots.
[04:49] Evan: Back to numbers — can you give a rough per-token estimate now so we can sanity-check against the $15k cap?
[04:55] Priya: Rough quick math: using public-ish numbers as an example, with quantized 13B and good batching, you might land around $0.0008 - $0.0020 per generated token depending on batch hit and cache. At 650 tokens/request and 50k requests in a month (approx), that range maps to $26k - $81k, so we need to reduce either tokens/request, increase batching efficiency or pick cheaper model/quant.
[05:22] Maya: Hmm that's above our pilot cap. What levers do we have short-term?
[05:26] Priya: Short term: reduce avg tokens by truncating responses or using structured summaries; increase effective batching with small request coalescing (up to 8); enable prefix/KV caching to cut redundant generation; and use a lighter model for lower cost paths (e.g., draft answers) and a larger model only for high-value queries.
[05:42] Evan: We can categorize requests by value — most are low-value quick answers, 20% are high-value that need better quality.
[05:49] Jordan: Then a hybrid routing plan makes sense — classify and route low-value to a 7B quantized model and high-value to 13B. We'll model a split 80/20 and show cost/latency impact.
[05:59] Sofia: How long to run the bench and produce a confidence window for unit economics?
[06:03] Priya: For synthetic benches, 3 business days of runs across configs to get stable numbers. Replay tests with your prompts, 2 days. Live smoke test 1 day. Then analysis and a cost model write-up ~ one week to compile. End-to-end about 5 weeks; add 1 week buffer, so 6 weeks total.
[06:18] Jordan: That fits with our suggested 6-week pilot timeline. We'll break milestones weekly: week 0 onboarding & security, week 1-2 synthetic perf, week 3 replay, week 4 quality evals & smoke, week 5 analysis & recommendations, week 6 optional follow-up/hand-off.
[06:33] Liam: For security onboarding — we'll need an AAD SAML setup and RBAC mapping, plus KMS integration for keys. Is that supported for VPC peering?
[06:43] Carlos: Yes, KMS integration and SAML SSO are supported. For VPC peering there are a couple of networking checks. We'll send the security pack and a short network checklist.
[06:51] Maya: Great. One more on metrics — can you surface cost per session (user session) not just per token?
[06:55] Jordan: Yes we can compute cost per session by joining tokens generated per session with routing metadata; we'll add a sample column in the spreadsheet.
[07:02] Evan: On reporting cadence, we want weekly updates and a mid-point review after phase 2.
[07:07] Jordan: Agreed.
[07:09] [long silence / note: background noise]
[07:20] Priya: Quick note on batching — coalescing incoming requests requires low queuing delay. We'll tune coalescing window to 10-30ms to avoid violating the p95 target — we'll experiment.
[07:31] Sofia: If coalescing adds 20ms that's acceptable as long as p95 stays <250ms.
[07:36] Priya: Right. Also, KV cache helps more for long conversation histories — if you truncate context smartly you get cost wins without quality loss. We'll include heuristics in the recommendations.
[07:47] Maya: Will you run tests across different GPU types? We use AWS G5 and some A100s in other projects.
[07:52] Priya: We'll bench on Redwood's representative fleet (A10/A100-equivalent) and include extrapolations for G5. We'll note caveats.
[07:59] Jordan: OK let's surface explicit success criteria. From this call it sounds like: 1) p95 latency <= 250ms at expected peak, 2) average cost per generated token <= $0.0015 for production path after optimizations (pilot may be higher but must fit pilot cap), 3) quality regression within agreed thresholds on the 200-prompt eval set. Anyone disagree?
[08:20] Sofia: Agree.
[08:22] Evan: Agree.
[08:24] Liam: Agree.
[08:25] Jordan: Great. I'll summarize next steps and owners.
[08:28] [00:08:28 - Jordan recaps] Jordan: Action items: Redwood to send cost model template and bench plan, Priya to draft config matrix, Carlos to send security checklist. Harvest to supply the prioritized 200-prompt eval set and sanitized traffic sample. Schedule mid-point review end of week 2.
[08:46] Evan: We'll get those to you by Monday.
[08:49] Maya: Yes, Monday for prompts and traffic sample.
[08:51] Jordan: Perfect. Any final things?
[08:53] Sofia: Please include a quick example of routing policy in the deck — 80/20 hybrid plan.
[08:58] Jordan: Will do. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for milestone checkpoints.
[09:04] [call ends]
next_steps: Redwood to send cost model spreadsheet (template + example scenarios) - Jordan - within 2 business days
Redwood to share benchmark plan and config matrix (models, quant levels, batch windows, cache sims) - Priya - EOD Wednesday
Redwood to send security pack and VPC peering checklist - Carlos - within 3 business days
Harvest to provide prioritized 200-prompt eval set and sanitized traffic sample - Maya/Evan - by next Monday
Schedule mid-point review (end of week 2) and weekly status calls - Jordan - calendar invite by tomorrow
